data.narrative:
MATERIAL operates in Climate & Energy at the Seed stage with $7.1M in total capital raised (including a $1.25M USAF SBIR grant). The target sector comprises one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix. However, no peers matched filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier clustering, rendering peer-median analysis inapplicable.

Stage-progression methodology applies, using the $7.1M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.5x multiplier for progression from Seed to subsequent stage. This yields a median implied valuation of $18M. Sensitivity around this central estimate produces a range of $15M (low) to $20M (high), reflecting ±15% variance typical of early-stage step-up scenarios.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $15M–$20M, centered at $18M. This valuation is anchored exclusively to stage-progression mechanics; peer triangulation remains unavailable pending identification of narrower comparables at matched development stages. Key uncertainties include the company's pathway to revenue, technical de-risking of the fully 3D-printed battery platform, and USAF commercialization trajectory. The founding team's relevant domain experience (F1 design engineering, battery research) supports technical credibility but does not materially adjust the valuation range absent additional financial or market data.
